facts.fact: The health ministry's PNDIS II states that DHIS2 is implemented for collecting aggregate data at every level of the health pyramid, from the central level down to the health centre, as at the time of drafting in 2019.

The health ministry's PNDIS II states that data are keyed into DHIS2's web forms directly in every facility with a computer and internet, with no district encoders in between, which at the time of drafting was true of all hospitals and the majority of health centres; most facilities still compile the aggregates from paper registers.

The health ministry's PNDIS II says the majority of health centres key their own monthly reports into DHIS2 and only a limited number without power or, more often, internet still rely on the health district, but gives no count or share; it puts first-level facilities at more than 1,000.

The PNDIS II states that the ministry's Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire manages DHIS2 and has largely acquired the skills to run and develop the national implementation on its own.

The health ministry's costed PNDIS II for 2020-2024 names DHIS2, budgeting 1,312,000 euros for its health information system axis, of which 200,000 euros to extend DHIS2 access by training an agent in every health centre not yet keying its reports; the plan was drawn up in 2019.
The PNDIS II proposes financing the plan through a multi-donor common basket, which it describes as similar to the financing model already used for DHIS2; the plan itself was financed by Enabel.

The PNDIS II states that by mid-2019 a total of 16 public hospitals and 5 private facilities had been computerised with OpenClinic GA, implemented in depth in most of them and giving a single shared patient record.

The PNDIS II states that in the computerised hospitals OpenClinic GA runs on a local server in each hospital for clinical users, with data exchanged between clinical services, laboratory, imaging and pharmacy in real time without further manual entry; it does not use the words point of care, and the record stays on the hospital's server.

The PNDIS II states that a project to computerise three health centres fully with OpenClinic HealthCenter Edition, patient record included, was still under way at the time of drafting, against more than 1,000 first-level facilities; health centres must still keep paper registers alongside.

The PNDIS II states that an action-research project launched by the ministry in early January 2018 put two register and summary patient record applications, CERHIS and Heroda, into three health centres each, and that neither was continued: CERHIS never ran for more than a month and Heroda lacked DHIS2 integration and doubled the paper work.

The health ministry's costed PNDIS II for 2020-2024 sets the aim of computerising every hospital and half of public health centres by the end of 2023 with a complete standardised electronic medical record, names OpenClinic as the hospital system, and budgets 5,533,000 euros for that axis; the plan was drawn up in 2019.
